findings.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:72 — group.add pushes the user unconditionally, so adding a username already in the group raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique (500) instead of being idempotent like the old usernames= diff logic.

app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — params[:limit] is uncapped (previous 200 cap removed) and negative/zero values are not sanitised, so any user can request limit=10000000 on huge automatic groups (DoS) or limit=-1/offset=-1 which makes Postgres raise (500).

app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:70 — Unknown usernames (and entries with surrounding whitespace, e.g. "a, b") are silently skipped and the endpoint still returns success_json even when zero users were added, so the UI cannot tell the admin nothing happened.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:72 — group.add pushes the user unconditionally, so adding a username already in the group raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique (500) instead of being idempotent like the old usernames= diff logic.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `add_members` iterating usernames and calling `group.add(user)`, but it does not show the implementation of `Group#add` or the membership join constraints. Without that, we cannot verify that adding an existing member will raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`. Additionally, the pre-diff controller already used `group.add(user)` in `update_patch`, so this behavior (and any duplicate-handling) is not clearly newly introduced by this change. The finding relies on assumptions about code not present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — params[:limit] is uncapped (previous 200 cap removed) and negative/zero values are not sanitised, so any user can request limit=10000000 on huge automatic groups (DoS) or limit=-1/offset=-1 which makes Postgres raise (500).

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the new code sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` and then runs `group.users...limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no bounding or non-negative validation. This means a client can request an arbitrarily large `limit` (potentially causing heavy DB work plus huge JSON serialization) and can pass a negative `offset` (e.g. `-1`), which will produce `OFFSET -1` and can error at the DB level (500). The finding’s note about a “previous 200 cap” is slightly off (it was a default, not an enforced cap), but the uncapped/unsanitized parameter issue is real in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:89 — group.users.delete(user_id) on a has_many :through does a raw delete_all on group_users, bypassing Group#remove / GroupUser destroy callbacks, so the user's primary_group_id/title are left pointing at a group they are no longer in.

adjudication.rationale: In the new Admin::GroupsController#remove_member, the diff shows `group.users.delete(user_id)` is used instead of the prior pattern elsewhere in this controller of calling `group.remove(user)` (seen in the removed update_patch logic). In Rails, `has_many :through` association `.delete` removes join rows via a direct delete (no destroy callbacks on the join model and bypasses any custom logic that might live in `Group#remove`). So this change can skip important side effects/callbacks that previously would have run when removing a user via `group.remove`, making it a real regression risk introduced by the diff. The specific mention of `primary_group_id/title` being left pointing cannot be proven from this diff alone, but the callback/side-effect bypass is directly implied by the code change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:70 — Unknown usernames (and entries with surrounding whitespace, e.g. "a, b") are silently skipped and the endpoint still returns success_json even when zero users were added, so the UI cannot tell the admin nothing happened.

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, the code does `usernames.split(",").each do |username|` and only adds a user when `User.find_by_username(username)` returns a record. There is no `strip` on each `username`, so inputs like "a, b" will look up " b" and fail. Unknown usernames are also silently ignored. After the loop it unconditionally attempts `group.save` and, if it succeeds (which it likely will even with no membership changes), returns `success_json` without indicating that zero users were added. This matches the finding and is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:76 — Memberships are persisted by group.add before group.save is evaluated, so a validation failure returns 422 while the users were already added (partial failure with a misleading error).

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code loops `group.add(user)` and then checks `if group.save ... else ...`. The finding assumes `group.add` persists membership immediately and that `group.save` could fail afterwards, causing a misleading 422 with members already added. However, the diff does not show the implementation of `Group#add` or any new validation/transaction behavior that would make `group.save` fail here (the group is loaded from the DB and its core attributes aren’t changed in this action). Without `Group#add` semantics or a demonstrated failure mode, the “partial failure” claim is not verifiable from this diff and is largely speculative.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:89 — Removing a user_id that is not a member (or 0/garbage) raises RecordNotFound (404) rather than the previously specified silent success, and the stale client member list after a concurrent removal now surfaces as an error.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `remove_member` action, the code does not look up a `User` record at all; it does `user_id = params.require(:user_id).to_i` and then `group.users.delete(user_id)`. In Rails, `has_many`/`has_many :through` `association.delete(id)` issues a delete on the join/association scope and is typically a no-op if the id is not associated (or even if it doesn’t exist), rather than raising `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound`. Also, “0/garbage” becomes `0` via `to_i`, and `delete(0)` would likewise be a no-op, not a 404. The only immediate exception path introduced here is `params.require(:user_id)` (400 ParameterMissing) if the param is absent, which the finding does not claim.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:19 — totalPages uses floor(user_count/limit)+1, so when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 50/50) it reports an extra empty page and next navigates to offset==user_count returning zero members.
matched_golden_ids: In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.

The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same underlying bug: when the total user_count is an exact multiple of the page limit, the paging logic allows navigating to offset == user_count, which returns zero members and shows an empty last page (confusing UX). The candidate additionally mentions totalPages being computed with an extra page, but it still pinpoints the empty-page-at-end problem tied to offset==user_count.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:14 — limit is taken from result.meta.limit without validation; a limit of 0 (e.g. limit=abc coerced to 0 server-side) yields division by zero (Infinity/NaN pages) and next never advances.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:50 — removeMember/addMembers swallow ajax failures (no catch) and never surface the 404/422/500 to the admin, so failed adds or removes look like silent successes with an unchanged list.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `removeMember` and `addMembers` both return the `Discourse.ajax(...)` promise and do not attach a `.catch`, but they also do not "swallow" failures: a rejected AJAX promise will still reject/propagate. While the calling controller actions (`removeMember`/`addMembers`) also don’t attach error handlers, the claim that errors "never surface" and therefore look like "silent successes" is not directly verifiable from this diff alone (it depends on how `Discourse.ajax` and global AJAX error handling behave elsewhere). The only strictly provable fact here is "no explicit error handling in these methods/callers," not that failures are hidden.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:50 — After removing the last member on the last page, findMembers is re-run with the old offset which may now equal user_count, rendering an empty page instead of stepping back.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `Discourse.Group#removeMember`, the success callback calls `self.findMembers()` without adjusting `offset`. `findMembers` computes `offset` as `Math.min(this.get("user_count"), Math.max(this.get("offset"), 0))` using the *current* `user_count` property (which is still the old total until the AJAX response updates it). If you are on the last page and remove the last member (e.g. `user_count=51, limit=50, offset=50` then after removal total becomes 50), the subsequent `findMembers` request can be made with `offset=50`, which equals the new total and yields an empty `members` list, leaving the UI on an empty page instead of stepping back to the previous page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:28 — Public `/groups/:name/members.json` response changed from a bare array to `{members, meta}` with no versioning or compatibility shim, breaking any external API client or plugin that iterates the old array.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (which would return a bare serialized collection) to `render json: { members: ..., meta: ... }`, i.e., a different top-level JSON shape. There is no conditional branch, parameter, or versioning/shim to preserve the old array response. This endpoint is under the non-admin `GroupsController`, so any existing client/plugin that iterates the response as an array would break.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:24 — create`/`update` now read top-level `name`/`visible`/`alias_level` instead of `params[:group][...]`, so existing API clients posting `group[name]` silently create a blank-named group or have their update ignored (200 returned) rather than an error.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes Admin::GroupsController#create and #update to read top-level params (params[:name], params[:visible], params[:alias_level]) instead of the previous nested payload (params[:group][:...]). This is directly visible in the controller changes and is paired with the JS model now POSTing/PUTing an unwrapped JSON body. As a result, any existing client still sending group[name]/group[visible]/group[alias_level] will have those values ignored by the server. In #update, that can lead to a 200 success response with no actual changes applied (since params[:alias_level]/etc. are nil and the record may still save). The finding's claim that this would 'silently create a blank-named group (200 returned)' is less certain because create will set name to "" when params[:name] is missing and group.save may fail and return an error response, but the breaking parameter change itself is real and verifiable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:34 — PATCH `changes[add]`/`changes[delete]` incremental membership API was removed but PATCH still routes to `update`, so old clients get 200 success with no membership change and `visible` silently reset to false (line 38).

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the `update_patch` code path that handled `params[:changes][:add]`/`[:delete]` incremental membership updates, and `update` no longer branches on `request.patch?`—it always executes the new logic. In Rails, PATCH `/admin/groups/:id` still routes to `#update` by default for a `resources :groups` route, so old clients sending only `changes[...]` will have those params ignored (no membership changes) but `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` will still run; if `visible` is omitted (likely for old incremental calls), it will be set to `false` and saved, returning success. This is directly implied by the new `update` implementation in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:40 — usernames` param on create/update is now silently ignored instead of setting membership; clients relying on the old contract get a success response but no members are added.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes Admin::GroupsController#create and #update to read top-level params (:name, :visible, :alias_level) and no longer reads/assigns any usernames/group membership (previously params[:group][:usernames] and group.usernames were used). Now membership changes are only via new add_members/remove_member endpoints. As a result, requests that still send the old usernames payload will succeed (group.save) but won’t add members, i.e., the usernames param is silently ignored.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71 — add_members` assumes `usernames` is a comma-separated string; an array param (e.g. `usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b`) raises NoMethodError on `split` and returns 500 instead of 400.

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members the code does `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` and then immediately calls `usernames.split(",")`. If the request supplies `usernames` as an array (e.g. `usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b`), Rails will give an Array, and Array does not respond to `split`, causing a NoMethodError and a 500. The method does not validate/coerce the type, so this is a real input-handling defect introduced/visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — limit` is unbounded and `limit=0` returns no rows; the previous 200 cap for automatic groups is gone, letting a client dump every member of a huge automatic group in one request.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:21 — findMembers` now returns `undefined` when name is empty (was a resolved promise) and no longer resolves with the member array, so plugin code chaining `.then(members => ...)` breaks.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:62 — Discourse.Group.asJSON` shape changed (no `group` wrapper) and `createWithUsernames`/`saveWithUsernames` were removed without deprecation, breaking any plugin using these public model methods.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `Discourse.Group.asJSON` changing from a `{ group: {...} }` wrapper to a flat object, and `createWithUsernames`/`saveWithUsernames` being removed in favor of `create`/`save`. However, the rest of the diff updates core callers and the Rails controller params to match this new shape, so there’s no in-repo breakage evidenced here. The claim that this “breaks any plugin using these public model methods” is not verifiable from the diff (it depends on out-of-tree plugin usage), making the finding speculative rather than a demonstrated defect in this change set.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:88 — Membership modification of automatic groups now returns 422 whereas the removed PATCH path returned 403 (InvalidAccess), a status-code contract change for clients.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the PATCH-based membership update path (`update_patch`) which raised `Discourse::InvalidAccess` for automatic groups (typically resulting in a 403), and replaces membership changes with `add_members`/`remove_member` actions. Both new actions explicitly `return can_not_modify_automatic if group.automatic`, and `can_not_modify_automatic` renders status 422. This is a verifiable HTTP status behavior change for the same “cannot modify automatic group membership” condition, which could break clients relying on the prior 403 contract.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:115 — Spec calls `remove_member` via PUT although the route is DELETE-only; controller specs bypass routing so the actual DELETE contract (body params parsed for DELETE) is not exercised.

app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:19 — totalPages uses floor(user_count/limit)+1 so when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 50/50) it reports an extra empty page and next() can navigate to offset==user_count.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `totalPages` in `admin-group.js.es6` as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` (when `user_count != 0`). For an exact multiple (e.g. `user_count=50`, `limit=50`), this yields 2 pages instead of 1. Because `showingLast` compares `currentPage` to this incorrect `totalPages`, the `next` action remains enabled on the real last page. `next()` then sets `offset = Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)`, allowing `offset == user_count` (50), and `Group.findMembers()` uses that offset and requests members with `offset=50`, which the server will return as an empty page (since `limit(...).offset(50)` on 50 total users yields no rows). This is a concrete off-by-one pagination bug introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6:11 — Public group members page now only ever loads the first `limit` (50) members with no pagination controls, silently truncating larger non-automatic groups that previously listed everyone.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` to always apply `limit`/`offset` with a default `limit` of 50 for *all* groups (`limit = (params[:limit] || 50)`, then `.limit(limit).offset(offset)`), whereas previously only automatic groups were paginated and non-automatic groups returned the full ordered list. On the public members route (`app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6`), it now calls `model.findMembers()` (which uses `limit: 50, offset: 0` by default) and the template iterates `{{#each m in members}}` with no added pagination UI/controls in `group/members.hbs`. No other pagination mechanism for the public members page is introduced in the diff, so larger non-automatic groups will be silently truncated to the first 50 members.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:87 — group.users.delete(user_id) on a has_many :through only removes the join row (find raises 404 for non-members) and bypasses Group#remove/GroupUser callbacks, so primary_group_id/title cleanup no longer happens.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes member removal in `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member` to `group.users.delete(user_id)` instead of the previously used `group.remove(user)` (seen in the removed `update_patch` logic). In Rails, `has_many :through` association `delete` typically removes join rows directly (often via `delete_all`) and can bypass any custom `Group#remove` logic and/or callbacks on the join model that would run with a proper `destroy`/custom removal path. So the core concern (bypassing intended removal behavior) is a real, reviewable regression introduced by this diff. However, the finding’s claim that it “raises 404 for non-members” is not supported by the diff—`delete` is generally silent when the association doesn’t exist, and this controller doesn’t raise 404 in that case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:65 — add_members calls group.add for usernames that are already members, which hits the group_users uniqueness constraint and returns a 500 instead of a clean error/no-op.

app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — limit/offset are not validated: limit=0 yields no rows and is echoed back in meta so client currentPage divides by zero (NaN), and a negative offset raises a Postgres error (500).

adjudication.rationale: In app/controllers/groups_controller.rb#members the diff sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` and then blindly applies `limit(limit).offset(offset)` and echoes both back in `meta`. There is no clamping/validation to ensure `limit > 0` and `offset >= 0`. If the client (or any caller) supplies `limit=0`, the response will return `meta.limit: 0`; the new client-side code computes `currentPage` and `totalPages` by dividing by `this.get("limit")`, which will produce `NaN/Infinity` and break pagination logic. If `offset` is negative (e.g. -1), ActiveRecord `offset(-1)` can raise an exception (commonly `ArgumentError`), resulting in a 500. These issues are directly introduced/allowed by the changed code paths in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:29 — findMembers clamps offset with the stale pre-request user_count, so after removeMember deletes the last item on the final page the reload requests offset==user_count and shows an empty page with currentPage > totalPages.

app/assets/javascripts/admin/routes/admin_group_route.js:13 — findMembers() promise is neither returned nor error-handled (previously awaited in afterModel), so member-load failures are swallowed and the page renders with stale/empty members.
matched_golden_ids: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that findMembers() became asynchronous and its promise is not properly handled/awaited/returned, meaning the controller/route may proceed before member data is available (race condition) and errors can be swallowed, leading to empty or stale members.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:32 — usernames is not cleared after addMembers (per the TODO), so a second click re-submits the same usernames and triggers the duplicate-member failure.

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, the `addMembers` action contains `// TODO: should clear the input` and only calls `this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"));` without resetting `this.usernames` afterward. That means the usernames text remains populated, and clicking “Add” again will resend the same usernames. The diff does not show whether the backend rejects duplicates or treats them idempotently, so the specific claim about a “duplicate-member failure” is not verifiable here, but the core issue (input not being cleared leading to repeated submission) is real and explicitly acknowledged by the TODO.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:6 — Pagination math (currentPage/totalPages/offset clamping) lives in the admin controller while offset/limit/user_count state lives on the Group model; the non-admin group-members route shares the model but gets no paging, so this logic will be duplicated when it does.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does place paging state (limit/offset/user_count) on `Discourse.Group` while computing `currentPage/totalPages/showingFirst/showingLast` in the admin controller, and the non-admin `group-members` route now calls `model.findMembers()` without any paging UI. However, the proposed finding is about potential future duplication (“when it does” add paging) rather than a concrete defect introduced by this change. Nothing in the diff shows duplicated logic, incorrect behavior, or a requirement that the non-admin route must page now. This is an architectural preference/speculation, not a verifiable problem in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:13 — totalPages uses floor(count/limit)+1, which yields an extra empty page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit; should use Math.ceil.

adjudication.rationale: In admin-group.js.es6, totalPages is computed as Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 (when user_count > 0). If user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g., 100 users with limit 50), this returns 3 instead of 2. This can lead to navigation to an extra empty page (next action can set offset to user_count, and findMembers uses that offset), so Math.ceil(user_count / limit) would be correct.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:10 — Page size 50 is hardcoded both as `limit: 50` here and as the default `params[:limit] || 50` in app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22; changing one silently desynchronizes the other.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce two separate defaults of 50 (JS model `limit: 50` and Rails controller `limit = (params[:limit] || 50)`), but this is not a verifiable defect: the client explicitly sends `limit: this.get("limit")` on every `findMembers()` call, so the server-side default is only used when the client omits the parameter. Having duplicated defaults is a maintainability concern, not a correctness/security bug demonstrated by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6:11 — findMembers() is fired without returning/awaiting its promise in both this route and admin_group_route.js:13, so the page renders with an empty members list and the previous afterModel-based loading pattern is abandoned.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:21 — findMembers returns undefined instead of a resolved promise on the empty-name early return, so callers that chain .then() (controller next/previous actions return it) get inconsistent types.
matched_golden_ids: Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that the function has a code path (the empty-name early return) that does not return a value, resulting in `undefined` being returned instead of the expected value/promise. This matches the golden issue of missing explicit returns on all paths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:44 — removeMember/addMembers/create/save/destroy each hand-roll Discourse.ajax URLs to /admin/groups; the model now mixes public (/groups/:name) and admin (/admin/groups/:id) endpoints with no shared helper.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show Discourse.Group using both public (findMembers hits `/groups/:name/members.json`) and admin endpoints (create/save/destroy/addMembers/removeMember hit `/admin/groups/...`). However, the proposed finding is about lack of a shared URL/helper and “mixing endpoints,” which is a maintainability/architecture preference, not a verifiable bug/correctness/security defect introduced by the change. Nothing in the diff indicates these URLs are wrong or that this mixing causes incorrect behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:62 — Shipped TODO ("should clear the input") leaves the usernames field populated after addMembers, and `usernames` is now a plain controller property with no reset path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an `addMembers` action in `admin-group.js.es6` with an inline comment `// TODO: should clear the input`, but the action only calls `this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"))` and never resets `this.usernames` afterward. At the same time, `usernames` is changed from a computed property (previously derived from `members`) to a plain controller property (`usernames: null`) bound to the `{{user-selector usernames=usernames}}` input in `group.hbs`. Nothing in the diff clears that bound value on success, so the input will remain populated after adding members, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:101 — Private/protected methods were re-indented by an extra level here and in app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:40, diverging from the 2-space style used before this change in the same files.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show extra indentation for method definitions under `protected`/`private` in both controllers (e.g., `def can_not_modify_automatic` in `Admin::GroupsController` and `def find_group` in `GroupsController` are indented an extra level). However, this is purely a formatting/style inconsistency; it does not change Ruby semantics, introduce a bug, or create a correctness/security defect. The proposed finding is therefore a style nit, not a real problem per the instructions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:70 — add_members duplicates the username-splitting/User.find_by_username loop that the removed Group#usernames= setter already encapsulated, instead of reusing model logic.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `Admin::GroupsController#add_members` manually splitting `usernames` and calling `User.find_by_username`/`group.add`. While this may duplicate logic that *might* exist elsewhere (e.g., a `Group#usernames=` setter), that model logic is not shown in this diff and therefore cannot be verified here. Also, duplication/reuse is a design/style concern rather than a clear bug, security issue, or correctness defect introduced by the change. The new code is internally consistent and has corresponding tests for adding members.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/admin/admin_base.scss:164 — Form styles were moved out of the badges section into a shared `.groups, .badges` block, but a separate `.groups` block is added at line 463; the two group rulesets should be consolidated.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a shared `.groups, .badges { .form-horizontal { ... } }` block and later adds a separate `.groups { ... }` block for group-specific UI elements (`.ac-wrap`, `.next/.previous`, `.btn.add`). Having two `.groups` rulesets is valid SCSS and not a functional/correctness defect; they target different selectors and don’t conflict. The suggestion to consolidate is a maintainability/style preference rather than a verifiable problem introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/admin/admin_base.scss:465 — Four new `!important` overrides (.ac-wrap width, .item margin, .next/.previous color) to fight autocomplete styles rather than scoping selectors properly.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add several new `!important` rules in `admin_base.scss` under `.groups` (e.g., `.ac-wrap { width: 100% !important; }`, `.item { margin-right: 0 !important; }`, `.next, .previous { color: #333 !important; }`). However, the finding’s claim that these are specifically “to fight autocomplete styles rather than scoping selectors properly” is not verifiable from the diff and is largely a CSS-style/maintainability critique rather than a clear functional bug or defect introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/group.hbs:22 — Template reads `members`, `offset`, `limit`, `user_count` directly off the model via ObjectController proxying, coupling the view to raw ajax response field names (meta.total etc.).

adjudication.rationale: In `admin/templates/group.hbs` the template references `members` and `user_count` (and uses controller-computed `currentPage/totalPages` which depend on `offset/limit`). Those properties are intentionally part of `Discourse.Group` in this diff: `limit`, `offset`, and `user_count` are defined on the model, and `findMembers()` maps the AJAX response (`result.meta.total/limit/offset`, `result.members`) into those model properties via `setProperties({ user_count, limit, offset, members })`. So the template is not coupled to the raw response keys like `meta.total`; it only uses stable model properties. Using ObjectController proxying to access model properties is expected Ember behavior here and does not constitute a verifiable bug/defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — limit` is taken from params with no upper bound (and no lower bound), so `?limit=1000000` (or a negative value, which Rails treats as no limit) loads and serializes an entire group's membership in one request on a public endpoint.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and uses it directly in `group.users...limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no clamping. This allows a requester to pass an arbitrarily large `limit` (e.g., 1000000) causing a very large query and serialization. Additionally, a negative `limit` can result in effectively unbounded results depending on DB/AR behavior (e.g., PostgreSQL `LIMIT -1` meaning “no limit”). The endpoint is protected by `guardian.ensure_can_see!`, but it is still user-controlled input on a non-admin route and can be abused for excessive load. This issue is directly present in the shown diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:25 — group.users.count` issues a separate COUNT over group_users on every page request even though `Group#user_count` is already maintained on the group row; this is a redundant full-index scan per page load for large automatic groups (e.g. trust_level_0).

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff introduces `total = group.users.count` and returns it in `meta.total`. That line will issue an extra `SELECT COUNT(*) ...` query against the group_users/users join per request, in addition to the paginated `limit/offset` query immediately after. Given that groups elsewhere are already serialized with a `user_count` attribute (implying a cached/group-level count exists), this is a verifiable redundant counting query introduced by the change, and it can be a performance issue for large groups.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:26 — group.users.order(:username_lower)` is paginated without a select or includes for what GroupUserSerializer needs (avatar/uploaded_avatar_id etc.), so any per-user association in the serializer becomes an N+1 across the page.

adjudication.rationale: The diff in app/controllers/groups_controller.rb changes the members action to paginate `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)` and serialize via `GroupUserSerializer`, but the proposed N+1 claim depends on what `GroupUserSerializer` reads (associations vs. plain columns). The serializer implementation is not shown/modified in this diff, and the query already returns `User` records (so avatar-related fields could be columns on `users` and not require extra queries). Without evidence in the diff that the serializer triggers per-user association lookups, the N+1 assertion is speculative and not a verifiable defect introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71 — usernames.split(",")` is unbounded and each username triggers a separate `User.find_by_username` SELECT plus a per-user `group.add` (INSERT/uniqueness check), so a large paste of usernames produces 2N+ queries instead of one `User.where(username_lower: ...)` lookup and bulk insert.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, Admin::GroupsController#add_members assigns `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` and then iterates `usernames.split(",")` calling `User.find_by_username(username)` for each entry and `group.add(user)` per found user. This is verifiably an N-per-username query pattern (at least N SELECTs, plus per-user membership writes/uniqueness checks), and the split/loop is not bounded in code, so a large pasted list will scale poorly compared to a single `WHERE username_lower IN (...)` lookup and batched membership insert.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:72 — User.find_by_username` is called with the raw, untrimmed username; whitespace around comma-separated names (as produced by the user-selector) causes lookup misses and wasted queries rather than matching via `username_lower`.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code does `usernames.split(",").each do |username|` and then calls `User.find_by_username(username)` without trimming each token. If the incoming `usernames` param contains comma-separated values with surrounding whitespace (e.g. "bob, alice"), the second lookup will be for " alice" and will not match, causing missed additions and extra queries. This behavior is directly visible in the diff; there is no `strip` on each username element.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:47 — removeMember` and `addMembers` each refetch the whole current page via `findMembers()` after mutating, instead of updating the local `members` array; every single removal costs a full members + count round-trip.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that `removeMember` and `addMembers` both call `self.findMembers()` in their success callbacks, which triggers an extra `/groups/:name/members.json` request to reload the current page and meta (total/limit/offset). However, this is a performance/optimization suggestion rather than a clear bug or correctness defect: refetching is plausibly intentional to keep `user_count`, pagination state, and the displayed `members` consistent with the server after mutations. The finding therefore doesn’t identify a definite problem introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:10 — Client hardcodes `limit: 50` and `user_count: 0`, but `findMembers` clamps `offset` to `Math.min(user_count, offset)`; since server `meta.total` is trusted verbatim and `limit` is echoed back unbounded, a manipulated response or larger default silently changes page size with no client-side cap.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that `Group.findMembers()` blindly applies `result.meta.total`/`meta.limit` back onto the client model (`self.setProperties({ user_count: ..., limit: ... })`) with no client-side cap. However, the proposed issue hinges on a “manipulated response”/untrusted server data scenario, which is speculative and not a verifiable defect introduced by this change: the server is the authority for `meta.*`, and the client accepting the server’s chosen `limit` is normal for pagination. There’s no concrete bug/security boundary shown in the diff that makes this a real problem by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:20 — Public groups#members response shape changed to {members, meta} with new default limit/offset pagination, but no spec covers the new shape, total count, or limit/offset params.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb#members`, the endpoint changes from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (an array response) to `render json: { members: ..., meta: { total, limit, offset } }` and also applies `limit`/`offset` pagination for all groups with a new default limit of 50. In the provided diff, no specs are added/updated to assert this new public response shape or the `meta.total/limit/offset` behavior, so the change is untested and could break existing callers expecting the previous array format. This lack of coverage is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:17 — totalPages computes Math.floor(user_count/limit)+1 (off by one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit) and no JS test covers currentPage/totalPages/next/previous logic.

adjudication.rationale: Real bug: `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. When `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g., 100 users with limit 50), this returns 3 instead of 2. This also interacts with `next`: it can set `offset` to `user_count` (via `Math.min(...)`), making `currentPage` become 3 and triggering `findMembers()` with `offset=100`, which will return an empty member list. The additional claim about lack of JS tests is not verifiable from this diff alone, but the off-by-one/pagination defect is directly present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:115 — remove_member automatic-group test uses `xhr :put` while the route is DELETE; controller specs bypass routing so the verb mismatch goes unnoticed and the route itself is untested.
matched_golden_ids: The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same verb mismatch: the spec calls remove_member with `xhr :put` while the route expects a DELETE request, meaning the test can pass despite not matching the actual route behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:52 — Tests hardcode group id 1 (Group.find(1), group_id: 1) assuming a seeded automatic group exists instead of fabricating one with automatic: true.

adjudication.rationale: The updated spec introduces multiple examples that directly hardcode an automatic group as id/group_id = 1 (e.g., `xhr :put, :update, id: 1 ...` then `Group.find(1)` and `xhr :put, :add_members, group_id: 1 ...`). Nothing in this diff ensures an automatic group with id 1 exists in the test DB for this spec, so the tests become order/seed dependent and can fail with `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` or not actually test the intended behavior. Fabricating an `automatic: true` group (or looking it up by name) would make the tests deterministic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:50 — "ignore name change on automatic group" only asserts be_success on a silent ignore; no test that update actually renames a non-automatic group or sets alias_level.

adjudication.rationale: The referenced spec (context ".update") does more than just `be_success`: it explicitly reloads `Group.find(1)` and asserts the name was NOT changed (`should_not == "WAT"`) and that `visible` was updated to `true`. So the claim that it "only asserts be_success on a silent ignore" is a misread of the diff. The rest of the finding (no test for renaming non-automatic groups or updating alias_level) is about missing test coverage rather than a verifiable defect introduced in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:91 — Removed "succeeds silently when adding non-existent users" coverage: add_members has no test for unknown usernames, duplicate/already-member users, or which specific users were added (only count == 2).

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the entire incremental membership update test block, including the example "succeeds silently when adding non-existent users". The new specs for `add_members` only assert success and `group.users.count == 2` for valid users, and do not cover unknown usernames, duplicates/already-member cases, or verifying exactly which users were added. This is a verifiable test coverage regression introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:112 — Removed "succeeds silently when removing non-members" coverage: remove_member has no test for a user_id not in the group or a nonexistent user.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove prior incremental membership PATCH tests (including “succeeds silently when removing non-members”), and introduces new `remove_member`/`add_members` endpoints. However, the proposed finding is only that there is no longer a test covering removal of a non-member/nonexistent user. That is not a verifiable defect in the implementation itself; it’s a test coverage concern. The new `remove_member` implementation (`group.users.delete(user_id)` followed by `group.save`) is likely to behave benignly when the user isn’t in the group, and nothing in the diff proves incorrect behavior without such a test.
